newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraq-Turkey pipeline testing begins-Turk ministry.
newsitem.headline: Iraq-Turkey pipeline testing begins-Turk ministry.

text.p: Turkey's Energy Ministry said Iraqi oil began to be pumped into the Iraq-Turkey pipeline around midday on Thursday as a test under United Nations supervision.
The ministry said in a statement that it expects oil to be pumped continually into the Kirkuk-Yumurtalik pipeline "within a week at the latest."
The ministry said that according to information which it had received, the Dutch firm Saybolt found Iraq's oil gauging equipment on the border with Turkey to be "adequate".

The visit by the Saybolt experts is part of preparations for the flow of partial Iraqi exports worth $2 billion in six months under a U.N. oil-for-food deal whose terms Baghdad accepted on November 25.
The ministry said it expects that the Turkish pipeline company Botas will receive revenues of around $50-55 million in fees for the passage of the oil to Turkey's Mediterranean terminal Ceyhan.
The Turkish part of the 986-km (616-mile) twin pipeline from Iraq's Kirkuk oilfields to Ceyhan is ready to work at full capacity, the statement said.
The pipeline has been idle since the U.N. trade embargo imposed on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
There is about 12 million barrels of oil inside the pipeline, 7.5 million of that being in the section through Turkish territory.
Market sources and some officials earlier said the oil inside could have deteriorated in time and be used to produce low-tier petroleum derivatives like asphalt and kerosene.
